title: Assemble scalar cone coordinates after extension by zero
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, K and L chain complexes of A-modules indexed by the natural numbers, and a an element of A. Suppose there are A-linear equivalences e0:K_0 -> L_0 and e_n:K_(n+1) -> L_(n+1) direct_sum L_n for all n>=0. Assume e0(d_K x)=d_L(e_0 x).first + a*(e_0 x).second for every x in K_1, and e_n(d_K x)=(d_L(e_(n+1) x).first + a*(e_(n+1) x).second, -d_L(e_(n+1) x).second) for every n>=0 and x in K_(n+2). Extend K and L by zero to cochain degree -n. Then the extended K is isomorphic as a cochain complex to the mapping cone of a times the identity of the extended L. No regularity, boundedness above in homological degree, or nonzero hypotheses are imposed.

source.place: Tags 0628 and 0629, differential-compatible scalar cone coordinates; read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0628 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0629. The generic complex assembly and extension-by-zero case are expanded from the displayed cone matrix.

proof.text: In cochain degree -(n+1) use e_n, swap the two coordinates, identify their product with the categorical biproduct using ModuleCat.biprodIsoProd, and apply the inverse of HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber.XIsoBiprod. Use extendXIso to identify the two terms of extended L with L_n and L_(n+1). In degree zero use e0 and the right summand of the cone; the left summand is zero because extended L in degree one is zero. In strictly positive degrees both sides are zero objects, so use their unique isomorphism.

For the differential from degree -(n+2) to -(n+1), compose with the cone first and second projections. Mathlib mappingCone.d_fst_v gives the negative prefix differential on the shifted source summand. Mathlib mappingCone.d_snd_v gives a times that source summand plus the prefix differential on the target summand. These are exactly the two components of the assumed higher-degree equation, in exchanged coordinate order. For the differential from degree -1 to zero the first projection has zero target and the second projection is exactly the separate degree-one equation. All differentials with positive target degree are zero. HomologicalComplex.extend_d_eq transports the original differentials to the extended complexes.

The resulting degreewise isomorphisms commute with all differentials. Apply HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents to obtain the complex isomorphism. The construction also works for a=0, zero modules and the zero ring, since it uses no cancellation of a scalar and no division.

from.place: Perfect-generation induction step: Koszul orthogonality forces the affine restriction to be the pushforward from the smaller open; Koszul orthogonality propagates to positive powers; A sheafified Koszul coordinate is a scalar mapping cone; step 2: assembling compatible last-generator coordinates into an extended complex isomorphism

lean.statement: theorem scalarCone_iso_of_coordinates (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (K L : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℕ) (a : A) (e₀ : K.X 0 ≃ₗ[A] L.X 0) (e : ∀ n : ℕ, K.X (n + 1) ≃ₗ[A] L.X (n + 1) × L.X n) (h₀ : ∀ x : K.X 1, e₀ (K.d 1 0 x) = L.d 1 0 (e 0 x).1 + a • (e 0 x).2) (hd : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : K.X (n + 2)), e n (K.d (n + 2) (n + 1) x) = (L.d (n + 2) (n + 1) (e (n + 1) x).1 + a • (e (n + 1) x).2, -L.d (n + 1) n (e (n + 1) x).2)) : Nonempty (K.extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat ≅ CochainComplex.mappingCone (a • 𝟙 (L.extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat)))
